title: Interleaved prefetching and content-addressable slab optimizer for cross-request KV reuse
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Latency-sensitive workloads frequently re-send similar prompt prefixes across interleaved microbatches. Current KV caching stores full prefix slabs keyed by opaque fingerprints which leads to redundant copies on GPU when slightly different segments are present. This increases GPU memory pressure and reduces effective throughput under continuous batching.

Proposal: Implement an interleaved prefetching layer combined with a content-addressable slab optimizer (CASO). CASO will store compact fragment descriptors (content-addressable hashes for token-span segments) in the host index; the runtime keeps a thin residency ledger that maps active microbatches to fragment references rather than full duplicated slabs. An interleaved prefetcher will observe the batching scheduler’s upcoming request skyline and speculatively stage only the fragment references most likely to be reused across the next N microbatches.

Key innovations: 1) Fragment-level content addressing (SHA-like short fingerprint + length + position tag) so similar but shifted prefixes dedupe without perfect alignment. 2) Residency credits and eviction pricing to trade memory for hit-rate predictability. 3) Asynchronous compacting compaction worker that merges adjacent fragments into GPU slabs when co-residency is detected to accelerate sequential KV lookups. 4) Tight integration with continuous-batcher so prefetched fragments are scheduled into GPU warm queues in an interleaved fashion (non-blocking) to avoid blocking short-tail latency.

Why this is different: Instead of pure prefix-level dedupe or global slab coalescing, CASO works at fragment granularity with a spec-prefetch horizon that coordinates with microbatch interleaving to maximize reuse while minimizing speculative memory occupancy.
tasks: Design fragment descriptor format and collision policy
Implement host-side content-addressable fragment index (memory efficient)
Add residency ledger and eviction-credit accounting to GPU manager
Implement interleaved prefetcher hook into continuous-batcher scheduler
Implement async compaction worker for adjacent fragment merging
Integrate metrics (hit-rate, speculative-resident-bytes, eviction-slip) and dashboards
End-to-end tests with synthetic interleaved workload generator
Benchmark on p4d/p100-equivalent queues and compare to baseline
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end system demonstrates >= 20% reduction in unique GPU-resident bytes for representative conversational workload (95th percentile session reuse) compared to baseline
Median generation latency change within +/- 5ms for microbatched requests; 95th percentile tail not regressed more than 10%
Cache hit-rate (fragment level) >= 65% on demo dataset and mis-prefetch rate < 15%
No correctness regressions: outputs identical to baseline when cache hits are used (unit tests for KV lookup determinism)
Rollout smoke tests and canary pipeline pass; fallback switch can be toggled within 5 minutes
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: casal.enabled=false by default
Internal canary: route 5% of traffic from staging workload to CASO-enabled workers for 48 hours
Metric gates: if speculative-resident-bytes > 2x baseline or tail latency increases >10% for 2h, automatically disable in canary
Broader canary: increase to 25% on successful run for 24h, validate cost/latency/quality metrics
Gradual ramp to Dedicated pools with percent increments tied to cost savings observed
Full release only after runtime-1.20 QA signoff and documentation in Console runtime docs
